raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> **Depends on #57733 and #62407 (merge those first); mypy/CI fail until they land.** This PR's diff is only the 8 direct-reload files. They import helpers that #57733 adds (`finalize_model_weights`, `discard_weight_parts`, `stash_weight_part`) and rely on #62407's kept parameter objects.
>
> Validated as the stack #57733 + #62407 + this PR + E1 (aoshen02/vllm#179) + derived-tensor in place (aoshen02/vllm#180), with same-weight direct reloads on GB200, NUPD=3. GSM8K is measured before and after, and every tensor is fingerprinted against cold start:
>
> | Model | Job | GSM8K pre → post | Tensors changed |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | DeepSeek-V4.1 | 40010 | 0.909 → 0.904 | 0/1709 |
> | MiniMax-M3.1 | 40013 | 0.951 → 0.951 | 0/3148 |
> | Muse Spark NVFP4 | 40042 | 0.839 → 0.838 | 0/3011 |
> | gpt-oss-120b TRTLLM MXFP4 (NUPD=2) | 39950 | 0.938 → 0.936 | 0/796 |

## Problem

RL weight sync reloads the checkpoint into a serving engine. The layerwise reload moves every layer to meta, materializes it again, loads the checkpoint and reruns post-load processing per layer. That costs a second copy of each layer at a time, and its correctness depends on per-layer completeness bookkeeping, so partial or reordered updates are hard to get right.

## Fix

`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` (registered in `vllm/envs.py`; the default stays `layerwise`) writes checkpoint tensors straight into the live model and reruns cold-start post-load processing once, at the startup addresses:

- At cold start, before `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL), record each tensor's checkpoint layout.
- `begin_direct_reload`, called from `initialize_layerwise_reload`, views every tensor whose layout PWAL changed back to its checkpoint layout, on the same storage. The loaders then write the checkpoint tensors in place.
- `finish_direct_reload`, called from `finalize_layerwise_reload`, clears the one-shot "already processed" guards and reruns PWAL for every module, then the model-level hook, as cold start does.
- `replace_parameter` keeps a parameter's address when PWAL changes its layout: under direct reload, the new tensor is written into a view of the existing storage when it fits.
- Refused at cold start: `draft_lm_head_quantization`. The quantized draft lm_head would be written into the target lm_head it shares.
- Refused at `begin`, before anything is modified:
  - no layout was recorded (also the case for pre-processed IPC weight-cache weights, already in runtime layout);
  - a storage is too small for its checkpoint layout.
- `sharded_rdt` refuses direct mode at init, because its replay plan is baked by a layerwise (meta) dry run.

**Delivery contract.** An update must deliver every checkpoint tensor of each module whose PWAL changes the tensor's layout or is not idempotent. Tensors without such processing, for example a frozen embedding table, may be left out and keep their bytes. **Nothing in this PR checks the contract**: until the completeness follow-up merges, a violation is not detected.

PWAL must keep every checkpoint tensor registered under its checkpoint name. This builds on #62407 (retire/alias instead of delete/rename).

**Known limitations.** Non-default MoE backends whose PWAL reallocates derived constants on a rerun are not yet refilled in place: TRTLLM FP8 per-tensor, FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4/MXFP4, CuteDSL, and compressed-tensors FP8 constants. They are fixed in the derived-tensor follow-up. Online quantization is supported by a later follow-up.

## Tests

- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_direct_reload.py` uses a toy model with the hazards found on real models: a parent-derived tensor, a layout change, a loader bypass, a consumed scale and non-idempotent packing. It checks:
  - a reload equals a fresh cold start bit for bit, at unchanged addresses;
  - an unsent table without PWAL keeps its bytes;
  - refusals leave the model untouched;
  - an aborted update can be retried;
  - parked weight parts are handled.
- E2E (GB200, NCCL weight sync, 2 updates, reload diff on), this PR on #57733 + #62407 alone: Qwen3.8 GSM8K 0.971 → 0.970, 0/1434 tensors changed (39863); Nemotron 0.853 → 0.854, 0/913 changed (39864). For the full stack, see the table at the top.

## Dependencies / merge order

#57733 → #62407 → this PR. The follow-ups stack on this one: completeness check → moved-address/host-float check → side-tensor detector. The derived-tensor in-place PR, the NCCL `empty_cache` fix and the loader-bypass fix are independent.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @aoshen02.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Went through this against the RFC tracker. Leaving out anything F2/F4/F5/F7/F8 or PR 5 already covers. A few things I think belong here though:

**1. Refuse online quant in this PR.** F8 adds support, but until then nothing stops it, and `finish_direct_reload` pops `_already_called_process_weights_after_loading`, which is the only thing keeping online FP8 PWAL (`online/fp8.py`) from re-quantizing already-converted bytes. Same shape as the `draft_lm_head_quantization` refusal; a test next to that one would be nice.

**2. Replaced param objects are silently treated as derived.** `_checkpoint_views` skips anything without `_ckpt_layout`, so if cold-start PWAL registers a new `Parameter` under a checkpoint name, begin skips it and the loader writes checkpoint bytes into the runtime layout (a same-numel transpose passes `default_weight_loader`). F4 snapshots at first begin, after this already happened, so it won't catch it. Could we record the names in `record_checkpoint_layout` and raise in `begin_direct_reload` if one now points at an object with no recorded layout? That makes the #62407 contract enforced instead of assumed.

**3. Failure state.** `test_retry_after_aborted_update_matches_cold_start` says the worker refuses to run a partly updated model, but I don't see that anywhere. Either add a minimal in-progress/failed flag that begin/finish set, or fix the comment and add it to Known limitations.

Smaller:
- Dispatching direct mode from inside `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` reads oddly, and the env is checked separately at begin and finish. A small `start_reload` / `finish_reload` that stores the mode on the model would be cleaner (#63599 has one in `reload/lifecycle.py` if you want to borrow it).
- `finish_direct_reload` searches for a `"cuda"` param; the engines already have `self.device`, could just pass it through.
- Popping the guard on every module also hits `MoERunnerInterface`, which sets it in `__init__` as a hack. Probably harmless, but limiting it to modules with a `quant_method` seems safer.
- `_view_in_place` bounds writes by `storage.nbytes()` rather than the tensor's own range, so it assumes nothing else lives in that storage. Fine if F4/F7 add an overlap check, just want to make sure it's tracked.
- Add `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE` to the ignored set in `compile_factors` so toggling it doesn't invalidate the compile cache.

_This review/comment was written by an AI agent (Claude Code) on my behalf._

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,302 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Direct weight reload (``VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct``) on a toy model whose
+post-load processing has the hazards found on real models:
+
+(a) a parent derives a separate tensor from a child's weight (MLA W_UK/W_UV
+    from a quantized kv_b_proj);
+(b) post-load processing changes a weight's layout;
+(c) the model's loader writes a weight without its ``weight_loader`` (MiMo);
+(d) post-load processing consumes a checkpoint tensor, which stays
+    registered as a retired parameter (NVFP4 ``weight_scale_2``);
+(e) post-load processing that must never run on converted bytes (packing).
+
+Invariant: a reload equals a cold start on the new weights, at the startup
+addresses.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.base_config import QuantizeMethodBase
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload import direct
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.direct import (
+    begin_direct_reload,
+    finish_direct_reload,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.utils import process_weights_after_loading
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import default_weight_loader
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import replace_parameter, retire_parameter
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+
+_MODEL_CONFIG = SimpleNamespace(
+    word_embeddings_untied_by_checkpoint=False, quantization=None, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+)
+_DEVICE = torch.device("cuda")
+
+
+class _Method(QuantizeMethodBase):
+    """Post-load processing given as a function of the layer; counts runs."""
+
+    def __init__(self, fn):
+        self.fn = fn
+        self.runs = 0
+
+    def create_weights(self, layer, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs):
+        pass
+
+    def apply(self, layer, *args, **kwargs):
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        self.runs += 1
+        self.fn(layer)
+
+
+def _derive_w_uk(layer):  # (a): a separate tensor derived from the child
+    w_uk = (layer.kv_b.weight.float() * layer.k_scale).t().contiguous()
+    if hasattr(layer, "W_UK"):  # refilled in place: graphs keep its address
+        layer.W_UK.copy_(w_uk)
+    else:
+        layer.W_UK = w_uk
+
+
+def _transpose(layer):  # (b): kernel layout differs from the checkpoint's
+    replace_parameter(layer, "weight", layer.weight.t().contiguous())
+
+
+def _requantize(layer):  # (c): fused-FP8-like rescale
+    scale = layer.weight.float().abs().amax()
+    replace_parameter(layer, "weight", (layer.weight / scale).to(layer.weight.dtype))
+    replace_parameter(layer, "weight_scale", scale.reshape(1))
+
+
+def _consume_scale_2(layer):  # (d): NVFP4 weight_scale_2 folded in, retired
+    ws2 = layer.weight_scale_2
+    replace_parameter(layer, "global_scale", (1.0 / ws2).reshape(1))
+    replace_parameter(layer, "weight", (layer.weight * ws2).to(layer.weight.dtype))
+    retire_parameter(layer, "weight_scale_2")
+
+
+def _pack(layer):  # (e): not idempotent, must never run on converted bytes
+    replace_parameter(layer, "weight", (layer.weight * 2).t().contiguous())
+
+
+_SHAPES = {
+    "attn.kv_b.weight": ((8, 4), torch.bfloat16),
+    "proj.weight": ((4, 6), torch.bfloat16),
+    "mimo.weight": ((4, 4), torch.bfloat16),
+    "nvfp4.weight": ((4, 4), torch.bfloat16),
+    "nvfp4.weight_scale_2": ((), torch.float32),
+    "engram.weight": ((3, 5), torch.bfloat16),
+}
+_PWAL = {
+    "attn.kv_b": None,
+    "proj": _transpose,
+    "mimo": _requantize,
+    "nvfp4": _consume_scale_2,
+    "engram": _pack,
+}
+
+
+class _Layer(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, fn):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.quant_method = _Method(fn) if fn is not None else None
+
+
+class _ToyModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.attn = _Layer(_derive_w_uk)
+        self.attn.register_buffer("k_scale", torch.tensor(0.5))  # not in checkpoint
+        for name, (shape, dtype) in _SHAPES.items():
+            *path, local = name.split(".")
+            parent = self
+            for i, part in enumerate(path):
+                if not hasattr(parent, part):
+                    parent.add_module(part, _Layer(_PWAL[".".join(path[: i + 1])]))
+                parent = getattr(parent, part)
+            param = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.empty(shape, dtype=dtype), False)
+            parent.register_parameter(local, param)
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights):
+        params = dict(self.named_parameters())
+        loaded = set()
+        for name, weight in weights:
+            param = params[name]
+            if name.startswith("mimo."):
+                param.data.copy_(weight)  # (c): bypasses param.weight_loader
+            else:
+                getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)(param, weight)
+            loaded.add(name)
+        return loaded
+
+
+def _checkpoint(scale: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    return {
+        name: ((torch.rand(shape, generator=gen) + 0.5) * scale).to(dtype)
+        for name, (shape, dtype) in _SHAPES.items()
+    }
+
+
+def _cold_start(weights: dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> _ToyModel:
+    """As ``BaseModelLoader.load_model`` does."""
+    with _DEVICE:
+        model = _ToyModel()
+    model.load_weights(weights.items())
+    process_weights_after_loading(model, _MODEL_CONFIG, _DEVICE)
+    return model
+
+
+def _reload(model: _ToyModel, weights: dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> None:
+    begin_direct_reload(model)
+    model.load_weights(weights.items())
+    finish_direct_reload(model, _MODEL_CONFIG)
+
+
+def _state(model: torch.nn.Module) -> dict[str, tuple]:
+    """Every parameter, buffer and tensor attribute: layout, bytes, address."""
+    tensors: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+    for module_name, module in model.named_modules():
+        prefix = f"{module_name}." if module_name else ""
+        for attr, value in vars(module).items():
+            if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
+                tensors[prefix + attr] = value
+    tensors.update(model.named_parameters())
+    tensors.update(model.named_buffers())
+    return {
+        name: (
+            (tuple(t.shape), t.stride(), t.dtype),
+            t.detach().contiguous().reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8).cpu(),
+            t.data_ptr(),
+        )
+        for name, t in tensors.items()
+    }
+
+
+def _assert_same(actual: dict, expected: dict, names=None, addresses=False) -> None:
+    """Layout and bytes (and addresses) equal, for ``names`` or every tensor."""
+    if names is None:
+        assert sorted(actual) == sorted(expected)
+        names = sorted(expected)
+    for name in names:
+        (layout, data, ptr), (exp_layout, exp_data, exp_ptr) = (
+            actual[name],
+            expected[name],
+        )
+        assert layout == exp_layout, name
+        assert torch.equal(data, exp_data), f"{name} differs"
+        assert not addresses or ptr == exp_ptr, f"{name} moved"
+
+
+def _ptrs(state: dict, names=None) -> dict[str, int]:
+    return {n: state[n][2] for n in (state if names is None else names)}
+
+
+def _runs(model: _ToyModel) -> dict[str, int]:
+    return {
+        name: m.quant_method.runs
+        for name, m in model.named_modules()
+        if getattr(m, "quant_method", None) is not None
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _direct_mode(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_RELOAD_MODE", "direct")
+
+
+class TestReloadEqualsColdStart:
+    def test_same_checkpoint_is_bit_identical(self):
+        model = _cold_start(_checkpoint())
+        before = _state(model)
+        _reload(model, _checkpoint())
+        _assert_same(_state(model), before, addresses=True)
+        assert set(_runs(model).values()) == {2}
+
+    def test_new_checkpoint_matches_fresh_cold_start(self):
+        model = _cold_start(_checkpoint())
+        before = _state(model)
+        _reload(model, _checkpoint(1.01))
+        after = _state(model)
+        _assert_same(after, _state(_cold_start(_checkpoint(1.01))))
+        assert _ptrs(after) == _ptrs(before)
+        assert model.nvfp4.weight_scale_2.retired  # as at cold start
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "names",
+        [
+            ["attn.W_UK"],
+            ["proj.weight"],
+            ["mimo.weight", "mimo.weight_scale"],
+            ["nvfp4.weight", "nvfp4.global_scale"],
+            ["engram.weight"],
+        ],
+        ids=[
+            "a-parent-derived",
+            "b-layout-change",
+            "c-loader-bypass",
+            "d-consumed-scale",
+            "e-not-idempotent",
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_new_checkpoint_hazard(self, names):
+        model = _cold_start(_checkpoint())
+        before = _state(model)
+        _reload(model, _checkpoint(1.01))
+        after = _state(model)
+        assert any(not torch.equal(after[n][1], before[n][1]) for n in names)
+        _assert_same(after, _state(_cold_start(_checkpoint(1.01))), names=names)
+        assert _ptrs(after, names) == _ptrs(before, names)
+
+
+class TestUnsent:
+    def test_tensor_without_post_processing_keeps_its_bytes(self):
+        # a frozen table the trainer does not send (Engram, an n-gram
+        # embedding): its module has no post-load processing, so a reload
+        # keeps its cold-start bytes; derived tensors read them as cold start
+        model = _cold_start(_checkpoint())
+        old = _checkpoint()
+        new = _checkpoint(1.01)
+        sent = {n: t for n, t in new.items() if n != "attn.kv_b.weight"}
+        before = _state(model)
+        _reload(model, sent)
+        after = _state(model)
+        _assert_same(after, before, names=["attn.kv_b.weight"], addresses=True)
+        expected = dict(new, **{"attn.kv_b.weight": old["attn.kv_b.weight"]})
+        _assert_same(after, _state(_cold_start(expected)))
+
+
+class TestRefusals:
+    def test_refused_begin_leaves_the_model_untouched(self):
+        # proj is viewed back first, in module order; mimo's storage is short
+        model = _cold_start(_checkpoint())
+        shape, stride, dtype, offset = model.mimo.weight._ckpt_layout
+        model.mimo.weight._ckpt_layout = ((64, 64), (64, 1), dtype, offset)
+        before = _state(model)
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="checkpoint layout needs"):
+            begin_direct_reload(model)
+        _assert_same(_state(model), before, addresses=True)
+
+    def test_draft_lm_head_quantization_refused(self, monkeypatch):
+        # the quantized draft lm_head would be written into the target's
+        spec = SimpleNamespace(draft_lm_head_quantization="fp8")
+        config = SimpleNamespace(speculative_config=spec)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(direct, "get_current_vllm_config_or_none", lambda: config)
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="draft_lm_head_quantization"):
+            _cold_start(_checkpoint())
+
+
+def test_retry_after_aborted_update_matches_cold_start():
+    # Direct reload has no rollback: a failed update leaves the model partly
+    # updated (the worker refuses to run it), and the next full update repairs it.
+    model = _cold_start(_checkpoint())
+    begin_direct_reload(model)
+    model.load_weights(list(_checkpoint(1.01).items())[:3])  # update aborts
+    _reload(model, _checkpoint(1.01))
+    _assert_same(_state(model), _state(_cold_start(_checkpoint(1.01))))

@@ -403,6 +403,16 @@ def init_transfer_engine(self, init_info: ShardedRDTWeightTransferInitInfo) -> N
                 "wrong expert slots. Disable EPLB or use another weight-transfer "
                 "backend."
             )
+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.direct import (
+            direct_reload_enabled,
+        )
+
+        if direct_reload_enabled():
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "sharded_rdt does not support VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct: its replay "
+                "plan is baked by a layerwise (meta) dry run. Use "
+                "VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise or another weight-transfer backend."
+            )
         # The worker is often a different install from whatever spawned it, so
         # check here too and not only where the actor options are set.
         check_ray_rdt_version()

@@ -318,6 +318,7 @@
     VLLM_DEBUG_MFU_METRICS: bool = False

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Direct weight reload.
+
+Instead of moving layers to meta and rebuilding them, the loader writes
+checkpoint-format tensors straight into the live tensors and the cold-start
+post-load processing runs once at the end:
+
+- cold start records each tensor's checkpoint layout (before post-load
+  processing);
+- ``begin`` views tensors whose layout post-load processing changed back to
+  their checkpoint layout, on the same storage;
+- ``finish`` reruns ``process_weights_after_loading`` for every module, as
+  cold start does. Post-load processing has to refill derived tensors in
+  place (captured CUDA graphs keep their startup addresses); nothing moves
+  them back.
+
+A reload is exactly as correct as a cold start on the delivered weights: no
+module is skipped because it "received nothing" (a loader may bypass the
+parameter's ``weight_loader``, and post-processing may read other modules'
+tensors).
+
+Delivery contract: an update must deliver every checkpoint tensor of each
+module whose post-load processing changes the tensor's layout or is not
+idempotent (it would convert the kept runtime bytes again). A tensor without
+such processing (e.g. an embedding table the trainer keeps frozen) may be left
+out and keeps its bytes. Nothing checks this contract here.
+
+Post-load processing must keep every checkpoint tensor registered under its
+checkpoint name (`replace_parameter`, `retire_parameter`): a reload loads it
+by that name.
+
+Selected with ``VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct``.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import torch
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm.config import get_current_vllm_config_or_none
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import _extent, is_weights_pre_processed
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+__all__ = [
+    "begin_direct_reload",
+    "direct_reload_enabled",
+    "finish_direct_reload",
+    "record_checkpoint_layout",
+]
+
+
+def direct_reload_enabled() -> bool:
+    return envs.VLLM_RELOAD_MODE == "direct"
+
+
+def _own_tensors(module: torch.nn.Module) -> Iterator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """A module's own parameters and persistent buffers."""
+    for n, p in module._parameters.items():
+        if p is not None:
+            yield n, p
+    for n, b in module._buffers.items():
+        if b is not None and n not in module._non_persistent_buffers_set:
+            yield n, b
+
+
+def _loadable_tensors(model: torch.nn.Module) -> Iterator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """Parameters and persistent buffers, each object once."""
+    seen: set[int] = set()
+    for module_name, module in model.named_modules():
+        for name, tensor in _own_tensors(module):
+            if id(tensor) in seen:
+                continue
+            seen.add(id(tensor))
+            yield (f"{module_name}.{name}" if module_name else name), tensor
+
+
+def record_checkpoint_layout(model: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+    """Cold start, before post-load processing: remember each tensor's
+    checkpoint layout. Runs once; reloads reuse the cold-start record."""
+    if getattr(model, "_direct_layout_recorded", False) or is_weights_pre_processed():
+        return  # pre-processed weights are already in runtime layout
+    config = get_current_vllm_config_or_none()
+    spec = config.speculative_config if config is not None else None
+    if spec is not None and spec.draft_lm_head_quantization is not None:
+        # after `begin` the draft's quantized lm_head is a view of the target
+        # lm_head's storage: post-load processing would write it there
+        raise RuntimeError("direct reload: draft_lm_head_quantization is not supported")
+    model._direct_layout_recorded = True
+    for _, t in _loadable_tensors(model):
+        if not t.is_meta and not hasattr(t, "_ckpt_layout"):
+            t._ckpt_layout = (tuple(t.shape), t.stride(), t.dtype, t.storage_offset())
+
+
+def _checkpoint_views(
+    model: torch.nn.Module,
+) -> list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """(tensor, view of its storage in its checkpoint layout) for every
+    tensor post-load processing re-laid out; raises if a storage cannot
+    hold its checkpoint layout."""
+    views: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = []
+    for name, t in _loadable_tensors(model):
+        layout = getattr(t, "_ckpt_layout", None)
+        if layout is None:
+            continue  # no layout: created by post-load processing, derived
+        if (tuple(t.shape), t.stride(), t.dtype, t.storage_offset()) == layout:
+            continue
+        shape, stride, dtype, offset = layout
+        storage = t.untyped_storage()
+        span = _extent(torch.empty_strided(shape, stride, device="meta"))
+        need = (offset + span) * dtype.itemsize
+        if need > storage.nbytes():
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"direct reload: {name} storage has {storage.nbytes()} bytes, "
+                f"its checkpoint layout needs {need}"
+            )
+        view = torch.empty(0, dtype=dtype, device=t.device)
+        view.set_(storage, offset, shape, stride)
+        views.append((t, view))
+    return views
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def begin_direct_reload(model: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+    """Make every tensor writable by its checkpoint weight loader.
+
+    Everything that can refuse the reload is checked first and raises with
+    the model untouched. Once this returns, the model holds checkpoint-layout
+    bytes until a finish succeeds."""
+    if not getattr(model, "_direct_layout_recorded", False):
+        raise RuntimeError("direct reload: no checkpoint layout was recorded")
+    views = _checkpoint_views(model)
+
+    # nothing above modified the model
+    for t, view in views:
+        t.data = view  # no zeroing: the full sync rewrites the checkpoint region
+    logger.info(
+        "direct reload: %d tensors viewed back to checkpoint layout", len(views)
+    )
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def finish_direct_reload(model: torch.nn.Module, model_config) -> None:
+    """Rerun cold-start post-load processing."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.utils import process_weights_after_loading
+
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()  # engines may write on other streams
+
+    # One-shot "already processed" guards would make the rerun below a no-op
+    # and leave the freshly written checkpoint layout in place.
+    for module in model.modules():
+        module.__dict__.pop("_already_called_process_weights_after_loading", None)
+
+    device = next(
+        (p.device for p in model.parameters() if p.device.type == "cuda"),
+        torch.accelerator.current_accelerator(),
+    )
+    process_weights_after_loading(model, model_config, device)

+def _extent(t: torch.Tensor) -> int:
+    """Number of elements spanned by ``t`` in its storage."""
+    if t.numel() == 0:
+        return 0
+    return 1 + sum((n - 1) * s for n, s in zip(t.shape, t.stride()))
+
+
+def _in_own_storage(old: torch.Tensor, new: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``new`` copied into the bytes ``old`` spans if it is smaller, so the loaded
+    storage is kept (with its ``data_ptr``); else ``new`` itself."""
+    storage = old.untyped_storage()
+    offset, size = old.storage_offset() * old.element_size(), new.element_size()
+    if (
+        new.numel() == 0
+        or old.device != new.device
+        or new.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == storage.data_ptr()
+        or _extent(new) != new.numel()  # overlapping or with gaps
+        or offset % size
+        or new.numel() * size >= _extent(old) * old.element_size()
+    ):
+        return new
+    view = new.new_empty(0).set_(storage, offset // size, new.shape, new.stride())
+    return view.copy_(new)
+
+
+def _view_in_place(
+    old_param: torch.Tensor, new_tensor: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """Under direct reload, a view of ``old_param``'s storage shaped like
+    ``new_tensor`` when it fits there, so the address survives a layout change.
+    None when it does not fit or ``new_tensor`` already lives in that storage."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.direct import direct_reload_enabled
+
+    if (
+        not direct_reload_enabled()
+        or new_tensor.device != old_param.device
+        or old_param.is_meta
+    ):
+        return None
+    shape, stride = tuple(new_tensor.shape), new_tensor.stride()
+    if any(st == 0 and s > 1 for s, st in zip(shape, stride)):
+        return None  # overlapping (expanded) layout: cannot be written in place
+    storage = old_param.untyped_storage()
+    if new_tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == storage.data_ptr():
+        return None  # e.g. a transposed view of the same storage: rebind keeps it
+    itemsize = new_tensor.element_size()
+    offset = old_param.storage_offset() * old_param.element_size()
+    if offset % itemsize or offset + _extent(new_tensor) * itemsize > storage.nbytes():
+        return None
+    view = torch.empty(0, dtype=new_tensor.dtype, device=old_param.device)
+    return view.set_(storage, offset // itemsize, shape, stride)
+

+def move_parameter(layer: torch.nn.Module, src_name: str, dst_name: str) -> None:
+    """Register the ``src_name`` parameter object under ``dst_name`` as well.
+
+    Both names then refer to one object and so to one storage: the loader writes
+    through the checkpoint name, kernels read the runtime name, and a later
+    `replace_parameter` on either name updates both. ``dst_name`` becomes the
+    name `kernel_parameters` reports for the object."""
+    param = getattr(layer, src_name)
+    existing = layer._parameters.get(dst_name)
+    if existing is not None and existing is not param:
+        raise ValueError(f"{dst_name!r} is already registered as another parameter")
+    layer.register_parameter(dst_name, param)
+    param.runtime_name = dst_name
+
+
+def retire_parameter(layer: torch.nn.Module, name: str) -> None:
+    """Mark a loaded parameter that no kernel reads after post-processing.
+
+    It stays registered with its loaded data (so it can be loaded again);
+    `kernel_parameters` and `get_live_param` skip it."""
+    getattr(layer, name).retired = True
+
+
+def set_kernel_parameter(
+    layer: torch.nn.Module, name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor
+) -> None:
+    """`replace_parameter`, for a tensor kernels read under ``name``: the parameter
+    is live even if it was retired before, and ``name`` becomes its runtime name
+    if it is registered under several names (see `move_parameter`)."""
+    replace_parameter(layer, name, tensor)
+    param = getattr(layer, name)
+    param.__dict__.pop("retired", None)
+    if hasattr(param, "runtime_name"):
+        param.runtime_name = name
+
+
+def _is_live(param: torch.Tensor | None) -> bool:
+    return (
+        param is not None and not getattr(param, "retired", False) and param.numel() > 0
+    )
+
+
+def get_live_param(layer: torch.nn.Module, name: str) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """``getattr(layer, name, None)``, treating retired or empty params as absent."""
+    tensor = getattr(layer, name, None)
+    if isinstance(tensor, torch.nn.Parameter) and not _is_live(tensor):
+        return None
+    return tensor
+
+
+def kernel_parameters(layer: torch.nn.Module) -> dict[str, torch.nn.Parameter]:
+    """The layer's own parameters as kernels see them: live parameters only, each
+    object once, under its runtime name (see `move_parameter`)."""
+    names: dict[int, str] = {}
+    params: dict[str, torch.nn.Parameter] = {}
+    for name, param in layer._parameters.items():
+        if not _is_live(param):
+            continue
+        first = names.setdefault(id(param), name)
+        if first == name:
+            params[name] = param
+        elif getattr(param, "runtime_name", None) == name:
+            del params[first]
+            params[name] = param
+            names[id(param)] = name
+    return params
+

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Went through this against the RFC tracker. Leaving out anything F2/F4/F5/F7/F8 or PR 5 already covers. A few things I think belong here though:

**1. Refuse online quant in this PR.** F8 adds support, but until then nothing stops it, and `finish_direct_reload` pops `_already_called_process_weights_after_loading`, which is the only thing keeping online FP8 PWAL (`online/fp8.py`) from re-quantizing already-converted bytes. Same shape as the `draft_lm_head_quantization` refusal; a test next to that one would be nice.

**2. Replaced param objects are silently treated as derived.** `_checkpoint_views` skips anything without `_ckpt_layout`, so if cold-start PWAL registers a new `Parameter` under a checkpoint name, begin skips it and the loader writes checkpoint bytes into the runtime layout (a same-numel transpose passes `default_weight_loader`). F4 snapshots at first begin, after this already happened, so it won't catch it. Could we record the names in `record_checkpoint_layout` and raise in `begin_direct_reload` if one now points at an object with no recorded layout? That makes the #62407 contract enforced instead of assumed.

**3. Failure state.** `test_retry_after_aborted_update_matches_cold_start` says the worker refuses to run a partly updated model, but I don't see that anywhere. Either add a minimal in-progress/failed flag that begin/finish set, or fix the comment and add it to Known limitations.

Smaller:
- Dispatching direct mode from inside `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` reads oddly, and the env is checked separately at begin and finish. A small `start_reload` / `finish_reload` that stores the mode on the model would be cleaner (#63599 has one in `reload/lifecycle.py` if you want to borrow it).
- `finish_direct_reload` searches for a `"cuda"` param; the engines already have `self.device`, could just pass it through.
- Popping the guard on every module also hits `MoERunnerInterface`, which sets it in `__init__` as a hack. Probably harmless, but limiting it to modules with a `quant_method` seems safer.
- `_view_in_place` bounds writes by `storage.nbytes()` rather than the tensor's own range, so it assumes nothing else lives in that storage. Fine if F4/F7 add an overlap check, just want to make sure it's tracked.
- Add `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE` to the ignored set in `compile_factors` so toggling it doesn't invalidate the compile cache.

_This review/comment was written by an AI agent (Claude Code) on my behalf._
